dimensions.evidence: In the case of any defendant convicted of a covered offense, the court shall, on motion of the Government or a victim, issue... an order prohibiting contact with a victim.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes lifetime legal restrictions on convicted defendants backed by contempt of court penalties, with fee waivers for victims.
dimensions.evidence: Such order shall remain in effect for the life of the defendant... A violation of such order shall be punishable as a contempt of court.

dimensions.evidence: Chapter 238 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following: Sec. 3773. Natural lifetime injunctions

summary: H.R. 8481, titled the Kayleigh's Law Act of 2026, establishes a federal legal framework requiring federal courts to issue lifetime no-contact orders against defendants convicted of certain federal violent or sexual felony offenses, upon the request of the victim or the government.

affected_groups.effect: Can request or consent to a lifetime no-contact order against convicted defendants at sentencing without paying any fees.
affected_groups.group: Victims of federal violent or sexual felony crimes

affected_groups.effect: Subject to mandatory lifetime no-contact orders issued at sentencing, facing contempt of court charges if violated.
affected_groups.group: Defendants convicted of covered federal felonies

key_provisions: Requires federal courts to issue a no-contact order at sentencing for any defendant convicted of a covered felony offense involving a crime of violence or sexual conduct, upon motion by the government (with victim consent) or the victim.
Specifies that the no-contact order lasts for the lifetime of the defendant unless terminated or suspended.
Prohibits assessing or collecting any fee from a victim for the issuance of the no-contact order.

Defines termination or suspension rules, allowing changes only if a victim files a motion alleging a pardon, commutation, or change in circumstances, or if a defendant files a motion alleging the conviction was dismissed or overturned.

Defines violations of the order as punishable by contempt of court and outlines a broad definition of prohibited contact including direct or indirect communication through physical, written, oral, or electronic means.
missing_information: Specific funding allocations or administrative costs for implementing the framework in federal courts.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8481, titled the Kayleigh's Law Act of 2026, establishes a federal legal framework requiring federal courts to issue lifetime no-contact orders against defendants convicted of certain federal violent or sexual felony offenses, upon the request of the victim or the government.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a standardized federal framework ensuring lifetime protections for victims of certain violent and sexual felony crimes through mandatory sentencing no-contact orders.
